problems.title: Glosten–Milgrom
problems.statement: V = 100 or 0 with ½ each; 20% of traders are informed.

problems.title: Market maker P&L

parts.prompt: Expected loss to the 20 informed traders (each wins 40)?
Expected gain from the 80 uninformed (each loses 10 on average)?

problems.solution: 800 lost, 800 gained: the spread exactly balances.

problems.title: Winner's curse
problems.statement: 5 bidders each get an unbiased but noisy estimate of a jar's value (true 100, estimate noise ±20 uniform).

parts.prompt: If everyone bids their estimate, the winner…

problems.solution: The winner's estimate averages about 113, so bid below your estimate.

problems.title: Conditioning on size
problems.statement: A client wants to buy 100× normal size, urgently.

options: widen and shade the offer up
work the order as agent over time
quote the normal 1-lot price for the full size
track post-trade mark-outs for this client

problems.solution: Price the information and impact; never give the screen price for the block.

problems.title: Mark-outs
problems.statement: After your fills with client X, the price moves 3 ticks against you on average within 1 minute; your spread is 2 ticks.

parts.prompt: Net expected ticks per fill (spread/2 − adverse move)?

options: widen for X or internalise less of X's flow

problems.solution: −2 ticks per fill: X is informed relative to your prices.

problems.title: Interview game
problems.statement: The interviewer has looked at a card; you make markets on its rank (1–13).

parts.prompt: They buy at your ask of 8. Update?
options: raise your market: they likely saw a high card

problems.solution: The trade is a signal; treat the interviewer as informed.

problems.title: Kyle intuition
problems.statement: An informed trader with a large order…

options: split it over time to hide among noise traders

problems.solution: Spreading the order out minimises information leakage and impact. Market makers watch for it.
